item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. and arrives in Spain
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year, left the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed.

item.title: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
item.description: Iran's U.N. envoy claims the U.S. military used Palantir and Anthropic AI systems to select some 2,000 targets over just four days.

item.title: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war
item.description: Russian government data obtained by pro-Ukraine hackers and analyzed by the BBC indicates that Russia has lost at least 490,334 soldiers during its war on Ukraine.

item.title: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
item.description: President Trump holds tens of millions in Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride of the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.

item.title: Security forces storm scene, end Colombia supermarket siege
item.description: Security forces stormed a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena, ending a day-long siege, with the nation's president saying all hostages were rescued and one captor was killed.

item.title: NATO allies anxious as war spreads beyond Ukraine, Russia borders
item.description: As Ukraine attacks Russian ships in far-flung waters, some NATO nations are voicing increasing anxiety over the war's spread to new regions.

item.title: Prince William and Kate's country home broken into, 2 arrested
item.description: Two men were arrested over a suspected burglary at the U.K. royal family's Sandringham Estate, the country residence of Prince William and Catherine, police said.

item.title: Army to detonate unstable lead explosives at Iowa plant today
item.description: The U.S. Army will detonate a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday, after days of back-and-forth between politicians and the courts.

item.title: Paperwork, not work, causing enrollees to lose Medicaid in Nebraska
item.description: Data from the months after Nebraska's early rollout of new Medicaid work mandates offers a look at the challenges enrollees in other states could face.

item.title: Small plane crash off Mississippi kills 6, including 2 children
item.description: Six people, including two children, have been found dead after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi, according to the Coast Guard.

item.title: Army to detonate unstable explosives in Iowa Wednesday morning
item.description: A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Iowa.

item.title: Maps show how far lead dust from Iowa detonation could travel
item.description: Maps of the planned lead azide detonation in Middletown show the shaded area stretching from near Burlington toward Macon, Missouri, by noon Wednesday. The forecasts will change with the weather.

item.title: Canadian astronaut's wife gives birth with husband aboard ISS
item.description: The wife of Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who is currently aboard the International Space Station, gave birth to the couple's third child, Canadian officials announced.

item.title: Iran developing chemical weapons, Israeli defense minister says
item.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Iran was developing chemical weapons and left open the possibility of preemptive strikes if necessary.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will petition to delay his execution
item.description: Nidal Hasan, the Army soldier who fatally shot 13 people in the attack at the Texas Army post in 2009, told a federal court Tuesday that he plans to file a petition to delay his execution by firing squad.

item.title: China launches first foreign astronaut to its space station
item.description: China has launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts, sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.

item.title: Police negotiating with hostage-takers at supermarket in Colombia
item.description: Around 20 people are being held against their will in Cartagena, Colombia, after a group of armed gunmen stormed a supermarket. This followed a botched robbery attempt on an armored truck. CBS News national correspondent Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Director of Iowa environmental group says plan to detonate explosives is safest path forward
item.description: The Army is set to detonate 5 tons of toxic bomb-making materials in Iowa on Wednesday, despite efforts by environmental groups to delay the explosion. Cody Smith, director of climate resilience at the Iowa Environmental Council, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Legal expert breaks down Trump's involvement in Huang reinstatement at Nvidia
item.description: CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson weighs in on if there are any Constitutional issues around President Trump's involvement in Nvidia's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: Where China stands in the AI chip race amid Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: Kyle Chan, a fellow at The Brookings Institute, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the status of China's chip development efforts amid Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: Angola inmates speak out against non-unanimous jury convictions
item.description: Reporting from the Louisiana State Penitentiary, 60 Minutes contributor Sebastian Junger interviewed inmates who are still in prison after being convicted by a non-unanimous jury, a practice the U.S. Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional in 2020.

item.title: Angola inmates convicted by a split jury speak out: "We're still fighting"
item.description: Reporting from the Louisiana State Penitentiary, 60 Minutes contributor Sebastian Junger interviewed inmates who are still in prison after being convicted by a non-unanimous jury, a practice the U.S. Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional in 2020.

item.title: Pope Francis' diary reveals he had visions of the devil, saw gates of Hell
item.description: The Vatican has released excerpts from Pope Francis' diary, revealing claims that the pontiff had visions of the devil and, at one time, saw the gates of Hell. Candida Moss, a biblical scholar, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Trump pushed for Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO over economic concerns, officials say
item.description: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday after resigning over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Officials say President Trump pushed for his return over concerns for the broader economy. CBS News' Arden Farhi and Nicole Sganga report.

item.title: Some AI-powered toys could offer up inappropriate, sexually explicit content to kids
item.description: Some of the hottest toys this holiday season are cute, cuddly and filled with AI. Mark Strassmann reports on how some of these toys could offer up inappropriate or even sexually explicit content to kids.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang still has security clearance, sources say
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche did not say whether federal investigators interviewed Jensen Huang — who was rehired as CEO on Monday — or examined his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: 11/24: CBS Evening News
item.description: Severe weather threatens Thanksgiving travel; U.S. spy agencies hit with cybersecurity breach.

item.title: 11/24: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche won't say if the Justice Department investigated Jensen Huang; airports brace for Thanksgiving travel rush.

item.title: Wendy's "pricing scheme" inflated menu prices, lawsuit alleges
item.description: In a proposed class action, a California resident alleges that Wendy's conspired with its franchisees to set and raise menu prices.

item.title: Some AI toys may not be safe for kids. Here's what parents need to know.
item.description: New AI toys, which use generative technology similar to that of chatbots like ChatGPT, have raised concerns among parents of the young kids to whom they're marketed.
